proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal M_N\) with \(\mu_D>0\).  Define
\[
A=D_T(1)-D_T(0),\qquad
C=\{D_T(1)>D_T(0)\},
\qquad
R=Y_T(1,D_T(1))-Y_T(0,D_T(0)).
\]
The target part of the no-defiers monotonicity assumption and the binary range of \(D_T\) imply
\[
A\in\{0,1\},\qquad A=\mathbf 1_C.
\]
By the target-cell contrast and target-ITT definitions and the law of total expectation on the finite set \(\mathcal X\),
\[
\mu_D
=\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}p_T(x)E_{P_T}[A\mid X=x]
=E_{P_T}[A]
=P_T(C).
\]
Here and below, versions of conditional expectations on cells with \(p_T(x)=0\) are immaterial because their coefficients in the sums are zero.  In particular, \(\mu_D>0\) implies \(P_T(C)>0\), so conditioning on \(C\) and division by \(\mu_D\) are valid.

We next show that the numerator vanishes off the complier event.  On \(C^c\), monotonicity gives \(D_T(1)=D_T(0)=d\) for some \(d\in\{0,1\}\).  The target part of the exclusion assumption then gives
\[
R=Y_T(1,d)-Y_T(0,d)=0\qquad\text{on }C^c.
\]
Consequently \(R=R\mathbf 1_C\).  Applying again the target-cell contrast and target-ITT definitions and the law of total expectation yields
\[
\mu_Y
=\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}p_T(x)E_{P_T}[R\mid X=x]
=E_{P_T}[R]
=E_{P_T}[R\mathbf 1_C]
=P_T(C)E_{P_T}[R\mid C].
\]
Combining the last two displays and using the target-CACE definition proves
\[
E_{P_T}[R\mid C]
=\frac{\mu_Y}{\mu_D}
=\theta_T
=\frac{\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}p_T(x)\delta_Y(x)}
{\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}p_T(x)\delta_D(x)}.
\]

It remains to prove observed-law identification of each relevant cell contrast.  Fix \(x\in\mathcal X\) with \(p_T(x)>0\), and fix any \(s\) such that \(x\in\mathcal H_s\).  The supported-cell mass and propensity-overlap assumptions give, for \(z\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
P_s(X=x,Z=z)
=p_s(x)e_s(x)^z\{1-e_s(x)\}^{1-z}
\ge p_0e_0>0.
\]
Thus all of the following arm means are functionals of the observed law \(P_s\).  Receipt consistency and known randomization imply
\[
E_{P_s}[D\mid X=x,Z=z]
=E_{P_s}[D_s(z)\mid X=x,Z=z]
=E_{P_s}[D_s(z)\mid X=x].
\]
Likewise, receipt consistency, outcome consistency, and known randomization imply
\[
E_{P_s}[Y\mid X=x,Z=z]
=E_{P_s}[Y_s(z,D_s(z))\mid X=x,Z=z]
=E_{P_s}[Y_s(z,D_s(z))\mid X=x].
\]
The receipt-contrast and outcome-contrast transport assumptions now give the explicit observed-law maps
\[
\delta_D(x)
=E_{P_s}[D\mid X=x,Z=1]-E_{P_s}[D\mid X=x,Z=0],
\]
and
\[
\delta_Y(x)
=E_{P_s}[Y\mid X=x,Z=1]-E_{P_s}[Y\mid X=x,Z=0].
\]
These equalities hold for every source covering \(x\).  Finally, the collection-support assumption guarantees that at least one such source exists for every \(x\) with \(p_T(x)>0\).  Since \(p_T\) is known, substituting these identified cell contrasts into the displayed finite sums identifies \(\mu_Y\), \(\mu_D\), and hence \(\theta_T\) whenever \(\mu_D>0\), as claimed.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
For every \(P\in\mathcal M_N\) with \(\mu_D>0\),
\[
E_{P_T}\!\left[Y_T(1,D_T(1))-Y_T(0,D_T(0))\mid D_T(1)>D_T(0)\right]
=\theta_T
=\frac{\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}p_T(x)\delta_Y(x)}
{\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}p_T(x)\delta_D(x)}.
\]
Moreover, every target-supported cell contrast is identified from each source covering that cell.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The frozen transport assumptions equate source and target cell contrasts only on the target support. For a cell having zero target mass, the source contrast need not equal the target contrast, although that cell has zero weight in the ratio. The corrected sentence makes this existing scope restriction explicit without changing the causal ratio claim.

proofs.proof_tex:
Put \(g_{sxz}(\theta)=E_{P_s}[Y-\theta D\mid X=x,Z=z]\) and
\[
 \psi_{sx,\theta}(O_s)
 =\frac{\mathbf 1\{X=x\}}{p_s(x)}
 \left[
 \frac{Z}{e_s(x)}\{r_\theta-g_{sx1}(\theta)\}
 -\frac{1-Z}{1-e_s(x)}\{r_\theta-g_{sx0}(\theta)\}
 \right].
\]
All denominators are positive by the source-support definition, supported-cell mass, and propensity overlap. Randomization gives
\[
 E_{P_s}\psi_{sx,\theta}=0,\qquad
 E_{P_s}\psi_{sx,\theta}^{2}=\frac{q_{sx}(\theta)}{p_s(x)},
\]
and scores belonging to distinct cells are orthogonal. The two transport assumptions imply, for every source covering \(x\),
\[
 g_{sx1}(\theta)-g_{sx0}(\theta)=\delta_Y(x)-\theta\delta_D(x).
\]
Consequently the target null contrast is the identified statistical functional
\[
 m_P(\theta):=\mu_Y-\theta\mu_D
 =\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}p_T(x)\{g_{sx1}(\theta)-g_{sx0}(\theta)\},
\]
where at each cell any covering source may be used. This equality follows from transport and the target-ITT definition; it is not a definition of the causal estimand.

Consider an arbitrary regular support-preserving path and let \(\dot\gamma_x\) be the common pathwise derivative of the residual contrast at cell \(x\). In source block \(s\), the Riesz representer of \(\dot\gamma_x\) is \(\psi_{sx,\theta}\). Hence a representer of \(\dot m_P(\theta)=\sum_xp_T(x)\dot\gamma_x\) has, after projection onto the closed span of these cell representers, the form
\[
 \Phi_a=\sum_{s=1}^K\frac1{n_s}
       \sum_{i=1}^{n_s}\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}
       a_{sx}\psi_{sx,\theta}(O_{si}),\qquad
 a_{sx}=0\ (x\notin\mathcal H_s),\quad
 \sum_sa_{sx}=p_T(x).
\]
The last equality is necessary because \(\dot\gamma_x\) may be varied separately for every target cell. Conversely it makes \(\Phi_a\) a representer. Any component orthogonal to the displayed span has zero derivative and can only increase variance. Independence of the source blocks and the preceding variance identity give
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_P(\Phi_a)
 =\sum_{s,x}\frac{a_{sx}^{2}q_{sx}(\theta)}{n_sp_s(x)}
 =W_{\mathrm{coll}}(P,\theta,a).
\]
The allocation polytope is nonempty by collection support. Its objective is continuous and strictly convex on its effective coordinates because \(q_{sx}(\theta)\ge v_0>0\), so its unique minimizer exists. Projection in the Hilbert space of product-experiment scores proves
\[
 \min_{a\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{coll}}(p_T,\mathcal H)}
 W_{\mathrm{coll}}(P,\theta,a)=V_{\mathrm{coll}}(P,\theta).
\]
At \(\theta=\theta_T\), the ratio identity gives \(m_P(\theta_T)=0\) and \(m_P(\theta_T+h)=-\mu_Dh\). Thus the local information for \(h\) is
\[
 \frac{\mu_D^2}{V_{\mathrm{coll}}(P,\theta_T)}
 =T_{\mathrm{coll}}(P).
\]

Finally suppose no source covers the entire target support, and fix \(s_0\). Choose \(x\) with \(p_T(x)>0\) and \(x\notin\mathcal H_{s_0}\). A support-preserving path can vary the common residual contrast at \(x\) in every source covering \(x\), leaving block \(s_0\) fixed. The derivative of \(m_P(\theta)\) is \(p_T(x)\dot\gamma_x\ne0\). A score measurable only in block \(s_0\) has covariance zero with that path score, contradicting the representer identity. This applies to every \(s_0\) and proves the non-subsumption claim.

Write
\[
 I_x(\theta)=\sum_{s:x\in\mathcal H_s}
       \frac{n_sp_s(x)}{q_{sx}(\theta)}.
\]
The denominators are positive by residual-variance regularity. Minimizing independently at each cell, the Lagrange equations give
\[
 a_{sx}^{\star}(\theta)
 =p_T(x)\frac{n_sp_s(x)/q_{sx}(\theta)}{I_x(\theta)},\qquad
 V_{\mathrm{coll}}(P,\theta)
 =\sum_x\frac{p_T(x)^2}{I_x(\theta)}.
\]
These formulas also cover cells having a single source.

Let \(b_x\) be the common perturbation of the residual contrast at cell \(x\). In a supported source-cell, the mean-zero conditional score
\[
 \frac{b_x}{q_{sx}(\theta)}
 \left[
  \frac{Z}{e_s(x)}\{r_\theta-g_{sx1}(\theta)\}
  -\frac{1-Z}{1-e_s(x)}\{r_\theta-g_{sx0}(\theta)\}
 \right]
\]
has derivative \(b_x\) for the arm contrast and conditional squared norm \(b_x^2/q_{sx}(\theta)\). Exponential tilting on the existing support, with the compensating latent-type tilt in the local-collection construction, preserves randomization, exclusion, monotonicity, source support, and the common contrast. Boundedness and the overlap and mass bounds make the Taylor expansion of each conditional log normalizer uniform. The product log-likelihood quadratic is therefore
\[
 \frac12\sum_x I_x(\theta)b_x^2+o(1).
\]
For a ratio displacement \(h\) at \(\theta_T\), the constraint is \(\sum_xp_T(x)b_x=-\mu_Dh\). Another Lagrange calculation yields
\[
 b_x^{\star}
 =-\frac{\mu_Dh}{V_{\mathrm{coll}}(P,\theta_T)}
   \frac{p_T(x)}{I_x(\theta_T)}
\]
and
\[
 \min_{\sum_xp_T(x)b_x=-\mu_Dh}\sum_xI_x(\theta_T)b_x^2
 =\frac{\mu_D^2h^2}{V_{\mathrm{coll}}(P,\theta_T)}
 =h^2T_{\mathrm{coll}}(P).
\]
The bounded compensations can change the quadratic only by constants depending on \(e_0,p_0,\rho_0,v_0,K\), and \(|\mathcal X|\); the bounds are uniform because these quantities are fixed. Thus the squared inverse testing radius is comparable to \(T_{\mathrm{coll}}(P)\). The calculation is also the dual of the exact allocation program, proving that the local necessity geometry is \(V_{\mathrm{coll}}\), including at allocation-face changes.

For a supported cell let \(a^{\star}(\theta)\) be the unique population minimizer. Since \(r_\theta\in[-1,2]\), propensity overlap gives
\[
 v_0\le q_{sx}(\theta)\le\bar q:=\frac{9}{2e_0}.
\]
Collection support, supported-cell mass, and sample balance imply
\[
 \frac{v_0}{N}\le V_{\mathrm{coll}}(P,\theta)
 \le\frac{\bar q}{\rho_0p_0N}.
\]
For the lower bound, Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
 1=\Big(\sum_{s,x}a_{sx}\Big)^2
 \le\left(\sum_{s,x}\frac{a_{sx}^2}{n_sp_s(x)}\right)
    \left(\sum_{s,x}n_sp_s(x)\right),
\]
and the last sum is \(N\). For the upper bound, assign every target cell to one covering source.

There are finitely many source-cell-arm strata. Applying the exponential Markov inequality to each bounded count shows that, outside an event of probability at most \(c_1e^{-c_2N}\), every supported arm count is of order \(N\). On that event, direct expansion of the ratios defining cell means and variances gives, uniformly in \(\theta\in[-1,1]\),
\[
 \max_{s,x}|\widehat p_s(x)-p_s(x)|=O_P(N^{-1/2}),\qquad
 \max_{s,x}\sup_\theta|\widehat q_{sx}(\theta)-q_{sx}(\theta)|
 =O_P(N^{-1/2}).
\]
Uniformity follows because the mean is affine and the variance is quadratic in \(\theta\). The objective is uniformly strongly convex after multiplication by \(N\). Comparing its empirical and population variational inequalities gives
\[
 \sup_\theta\|\widehat a(\theta)-a^{\star}(\theta)\|=O_P(N^{-1/2}),\qquad
 \sup_\theta\left|\frac{\widehat V_N(\theta)}
 {V_{\mathrm{coll}}(P,\theta)}-1\right|=o_P(1).
\]
No derivative of the optimizer is used, so this remains valid when its active face changes.

Let \(\xi_{sx}(\theta)\) be the centered empirical arm contrast. Transport and the allocation constraints imply
\[
 \widehat m_N(\theta)
 =\mu_Y-\theta\mu_D
  +\sum_{s,x}a_{sx}^{\star}(\theta)\xi_{sx}(\theta)
  +R_N(\theta),\qquad
 \sup_\theta|R_N(\theta)|=O_P(N^{-1}).
\]
Indeed, the common population contrast annihilates
\(\sum_s\{\widehat a_{sx}-a_{sx}^{\star}\}=0\), and the remaining product is \(O_P(N^{-1/2})O_P(N^{-1/2})\). At \(\theta_T\), the leading sum is a sum of independent centered bounded summands with variance \(V_{\mathrm{coll}}(P,\theta_T)\). Its largest summand divided by the standard deviation is \(O(N^{-1/2})\). Expanding each characteristic function to third order and multiplying gives, uniformly over the model,
\[
 \frac{\sum_{s,x}a_{sx}^{\star}(\theta_T)\xi_{sx}(\theta_T)}
 {\sqrt{V_{\mathrm{coll}}(P,\theta_T)}}\Rightarrow N(0,1).
\]
The normalized remainder is \(o_P(1)\), and the variance ratio tends to one. Therefore
\[
 \mathrm{AR}_N(\theta_T)\Rightarrow\chi_1^2
\]
uniformly for \(P\in\mathcal M_N\) with \(\mu_D(P)>0\). The third-order expansion gives an \(O(N^{-1/2})\) oracle distribution error; truncating the \(O_P(N^{-1/2})\) studentization error at \(N^{-1/4}\) gives a uniform \(O(N^{-1/4})\) error for the feasible statistic. Hence it is eventually smaller than \(N^{-1/8}\). Since the hull contains every accepted point, acceptance of \(\theta_T\) implies \(\theta_T\in C_N^{\mathrm{AR}}\). Taking the infimum over \(P\) and the lower limit proves the coverage claim and also places the procedure in the corrected finite-\(N\) near-honest class used by the minimax functional.

Put \(m_P(\theta)=\mu_D(\theta_T-\theta)\), as follows from the transported residual-contrast identity. Integrating the bounded exponential-moment estimates in the honesty proof gives random variables \(\Delta_N\) satisfying
\[
 \sup_{\theta\in[-1,1]}|\widehat m_N(\theta)-m_P(\theta)|
 \le\Delta_N,\qquad E_P\Delta_N\le CN^{-1/2},
\]
and
\[
 E_P\sup_{\theta\in[-1,1]}\sqrt{\widehat V_N(\theta)}
 \le CN^{-1/2}.
\]
The exceptional small-count event contributes at most \(Ce^{-cN}\), since the fallback price and denominator truncation make the empirical quantities bounded.

Let \(z_\alpha=\sqrt{\chi^2_{1,1-\alpha}}\). If \(\theta\) is accepted, then
\[
 \mu_D|\theta-\theta_T|
 =|m_P(\theta)|
 \le\Delta_N+z_\alpha\sqrt{\widehat V_N(\theta)}.
\]
Thus every accepted point, and therefore both endpoints of its hull, lies in the corresponding random neighborhood of \(\theta_T\). Since the whole interval lies in \([-1,1]\),
\[
 E_P\ell(C_N^{\mathrm{AR}})
 \le C_\alpha\min\left\{1,\frac1{\mu_D\sqrt N}\right\}.
\]
The deterministic lower variance bound \(V_{\mathrm{coll}}(P,\theta_T)\ge v_0/N\) implies
\[
 \frac1{\mu_D\sqrt N}
 \le\frac1{\sqrt{v_0}}
 \frac{\sqrt{V_{\mathrm{coll}}(P,\theta_T)}}{\mu_D}
 =\frac1{\sqrt{v_0T_{\mathrm{coll}}(P)}}.
\]
For \(P\in\mathcal M_N(u)\), this is at most \(v_0^{-1/2}u^{-1/2}\). Taking the supremum over the class and then the upper limit proves the stated uniform bound.

All source observations are iid within blocks and the two blocks are independent by construction. Randomization is independent of \((C,\varepsilon)\), consistency holds, exclusion holds because the potential outcome does not depend on \(z\), and monotonicity holds because \(D_j(1)-D_j(0)=C\ge0\). Both source and target ITT outcome contrasts are zero, whereas both receipt contrasts equal \(\mu_n\). Hence transport and collection support hold, although neither source covers both cells, and
\[
 \mu_Y=0,\qquad \mu_D=\mu_n,\qquad\theta_T=0.
\]
The supported source masses equal one, the propensities equal one half, and source shares equal one half. Thus the restrictions on \(p_0,e_0,\rho_0\) verify the respective assumptions.

At \(\theta=0\), \(Y=1/2+\varepsilon/(2\sqrt2)\), so
\[
 \operatorname{Var}(Y\mid X=x_j,Z=z)=\frac18,\qquad
 q_{jx_j}(0)=\frac{1/8}{1/2}+\frac{1/8}{1/2}=\frac12.
\]
More generally, independence of \(C\) and \(\varepsilon\) gives
\[
 q_{jx_j}(\theta)=\frac12+2\theta^2\mu_n(1-\mu_n)\ge\frac12,
\]
so residual-variance regularity follows from \(v_0\le1/2\). Every member property of \(\mathcal M_{2n}\) has now been checked.

Each target cell has only one covering source, so feasibility forces
\(a_{1x_1}=a_{2x_2}=1/2\) and all other coordinates to vanish. Substitution gives
\[
 V_{\mathrm{coll}}(P_n^{\mathrm{split}},0)
 =2\frac{(1/2)^2(1/2)}n=\frac1{4n},\qquad
 T_{\mathrm{coll}}(P_n^{\mathrm{split}})=4n\mu_n^2.
\]

For the divergence assertion, let the two outcome support points retain equal baseline probabilities. If \(\mu_n\le1/2\), change the upper-point probability of the complier receipt-zero outcome by \(-t\), and that of the never-taker by \(\mu_nt/(1-\mu_n)\). The control mixture is unchanged exactly, while the treated-arm mean changes by \(\mu_n h\), where \(h=t/\sqrt2\). If \(\mu_n>1/2\), change instead the complier receipt-one probability by \(t\); since \(\mu_n\ge1/2\), the same order bound results. The elementary inequality
\[
 \operatorname{kl}(1/2+t,1/2)\le8t^2\qquad(|t|\le1/4)
\]
then yields, after multiplication over the two blocks,
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(P_{n,h}^{\mathrm{split}},P_{n,0}^{\mathrm{split}})
 \le Cn\mu_n^2h^2.
\]
Thus pairwise observed-law divergence is bounded whenever \(n\mu_n^2h^2\) is bounded.

The causal, randomization, consistency, transport, support, mass, and balance checks are the same direct checks as for the split family. Every source has receipt contrast \(\mu_n\) and outcome contrast zero, so \(\mu_D=\mu_n\) and \(\theta_T=0\). For a source with noise label \(q_s\),
\[
 \operatorname{Var}(Y\mid Z=z)=\frac{q_s}{4},\qquad
 q_{sx}(0)=q_s,\qquad
 q_{sx}(\theta)=q_s+2\theta^2\mu_n(1-\mu_n)\ge q_s.
\]
Thus \(v_0\le q_L\) verifies residual regularity and both laws belong to \(\mathcal M_{4n}\).

For one cell covered by two sources with prices \(q\) and \(q'\), minimizing
\(qa^2/n+q'(1/2-a)^2/n\) gives
\[
 \frac1{4n}\frac{qq'}{q+q'}.
\]
In design \(A\), the two prices on each cell are equal, so the optimal mass is split equally and
\[
 V_{\mathrm{coll}}(P_n^A,0)=\frac{q_L+q_H}{8n}.
\]
In design \(B\), each cell receives one low-price and one high-price source, whence
\[
 V_{\mathrm{coll}}(P_n^B,0)
 =2\left\{\frac1{4n}\frac{q_Lq_H}{q_L+q_H}\right\}
 =\frac{q_Lq_H}{2n(q_L+q_H)}.
\]
Subtracting gives
\[
 V_{\mathrm{coll}}(P_n^A,0)-V_{\mathrm{coll}}(P_n^B,0)
 =\frac{(q_H-q_L)^2}{8n(q_L+q_H)}>0.
\]
All listed scalar summaries coincide by construction. The pooled-information theorem turns this variance inequality into strict inequalities of exact information, collection strength, and strong-branch length benchmark. Therefore a reduction retaining only those summaries takes the same value on two experiments having different information and cannot represent both. The differing datum is precisely the incidence of price with cell support.

For every feasible allocation, Cauchy--Schwarz and residual regularity give
\[
 W_{\mathrm{coll}}(P,\theta_T,a)
 \ge v_0\sum_{s,x}\frac{a_{sx}^2}{n_sp_s(x)}
 \ge\frac{v_0(\sum_{s,x}a_{sx})^2}{\sum_{s,x}n_sp_s(x)}
 =\frac{v_0}{N}.
\]
Since \(0<\mu_D\le1\), nonemptiness of \(\mathcal M_N(u)\) entails \(u\le N/v_0\).

Now use a support-split continuum. The displayed split family has
\(V_{\mathrm{coll}}=1/(4n)\) and \(T_{\mathrm{coll}}=4n\mu_n^2\). More generally, changing its bounded Rademacher amplitude and, if needed, choosing a propensity in \([e_0,1-e_0]\), gives a price \(q\) down to the class floor. The same calculation gives
\[
 V_{\mathrm{coll}}=\frac qN,\qquad
 T_{\mathrm{coll}}=\frac{N\mu^2}{q}.
\]
Choose \(q\) and \(\mu\in(0,1]\) so that the latter strength is at least \(u\). The bounded-outcome variance ceiling and the preceding necessary inequality ensure this for every nonempty strength class. Set
\[
 h=c\min\{1,u^{-1/2}\},
\]
where \(c>0\) depends only on the fixed class constants and is small enough that all Bernoulli tilts remain in their simplices. The compensated split construction, with a variance-preserving second-order adjustment if a residual-price constraint is active, gives \(P_0,P_h\in\mathcal M_N\) such that
\[
 \theta_T(P_0)=0,\qquad\theta_T(P_h)=h,\qquad
 P_0\in\mathcal M_N(u),\qquad
 \operatorname{KL}(P_h,P_0)\le C N\mu^2h^2/q\le Cc^2.
\]
The final inequality uses \(N\mu^2/q\asymp u\) and \(uh^2\le c^2\). Taking \(c\) smaller makes total variation at most
\(\eta_\alpha<(1-2\alpha)/2\). To verify this without an undeclared testing premise, apply
\[
 t\log t-t+1\ge\frac{(t-1)^2}{2(t+1)}
\]
to the likelihood ratio and then Cauchy--Schwarz; this gives
\(\|P_h-P_0\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\le\sqrt{\operatorname{KL}(P_h,P_0)/2}\).

Let \(C_N\) be uniformly honest. Its coverage at both laws is \(1-\alpha-o(1)\). Changing measure for the second coverage event and using the union bound yields
\[
 P_0\{0\in C_N,\ h\in C_N\}
 \ge1-2\alpha-o(1)-\|P_h-P_0\|_{\mathrm{TV}}.
\]
On this event an interval has length at least \(|h|\). Therefore, for all sufficiently large \(N\),
\[
 E_{P_0}\ell(C_N)
 \ge |h|\{1-2\alpha-o(1)-\eta_\alpha\}
 \ge c_\alpha\min\{1,u^{-1/2}\}.
\]
Taking the supremum over \(\mathcal M_N(u)\), the infimum over honest procedures, and the lower limit proves the bound.

For a general support face, the information-modulus calculation gives quadratic cost \(\sum_xI_xb_x^2\). Minimization under \(\sum_xp_T(x)b_x=-\mu_Dh\) gives \(h^2T_{\mathrm{coll}}\). Thus the split witness supplies the rate lower bound, and the dual cellwise tilts show that the necessity geometry on every face is exactly the collection quadratic program rather than a pooled scalar surrogate.

The profiled Anderson--Rubin interval is uniformly honest by the honesty theorem. It is therefore an admissible competitor in the definition of \(R_{N,\alpha}(u)\), and the length theorem gives
\[
 \limsup_{N\to\infty}
 \frac{R_{N,\alpha}(u)}{\min\{1,u^{-1/2}\}}\le C_\alpha.
\]
Conversely, the continuum theorem applies to every member of the honest procedure class and gives
\[
 \liminf_{N\to\infty}
 \frac{R_{N,\alpha}(u)}{\min\{1,u^{-1/2}\}}\ge c_\alpha.
\]
Both constants depend only on \(\alpha\) and the fixed class constants, and both inequalities are uniform over admissible sequences \(u=u_N\) with nonempty strength class. Hence
\[
 R_{N,\alpha}(u)\asymp_\alpha\min\{1,u^{-1/2}\}.
\]

Let \(a^{\star}(\theta_T)\) be the unique minimum-variance allocation and let \(\Phi_{a^{\star}}\) be the product-experiment influence score constructed in the pooled-information proof. Along a path with derivatives \((\dot\mu_Y,\dot\mu_D)\), quotient algebra, justified by \(\inf_N\mu_D>0\), gives
\[
 \dot\theta_T
 =\frac{\dot\mu_Y-\theta_T\dot\mu_D}{\mu_D}.
\]
Therefore the canonical gradient is
\[
 \phi_{\mathrm{eff}}=\frac{\Phi_{a^{\star}}}{\mu_D},\qquad
 \operatorname{Var}_P(\phi_{\mathrm{eff}})
 =\frac{V_{\mathrm{coll}}(P,\theta_T)}{\mu_D^2}.
\]
Minimality follows because multiplication by the nonzero scalar \(1/\mu_D\) preserves the Hilbert-space projection ordering proved for \(\Phi_{a^{\star}}\).

Uniform consistency of the profiler and the score expansion from the honesty proof imply, on every sequence with compliance bounded away from zero,
\[
 \widehat m_N(\theta)
 =\widehat m_N(\theta_T)-\mu_D(\theta-\theta_T)+o_P(N^{-1/2})
\]
uniformly for \(|\theta-\theta_T|=O(N^{-1/2})\), and
\[
 \widehat V_N(\theta)
 =V_{\mathrm{coll}}(P,\theta_T)+o_P(N^{-1}).
\]
Consequently the two roots of the local Anderson--Rubin acceptance inequality are
\[
 \theta_T+\frac{\widehat m_N(\theta_T)}{\mu_D}
 \mathbin{\pm}
 z_{1-\alpha/2}
 \frac{\sqrt{V_{\mathrm{coll}}(P,\theta_T)}}{\mu_D}
 +o_P(N^{-1/2}).
\]
These are the efficient Wald endpoints based on \(\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}\), up to \(o_P(N^{-1/2})\). If the fixed boundary of \([-1,1]\) is active, both procedures have the same first-order truncation. Taking the hull therefore does not alter the comparison, proving first-order equivalence and efficiency.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed: \(\mathfrak C_{N,\alpha}=\{C_N:\inf_{P\in\mathcal M_N:\mu_D(P)>0}P\{\theta_T(P)\in C_N\}\ge1-\alpha-N^{-1/8},\ C_N\text{ is a data-measurable closed interval in }[-1,1]\}\).
proposed_definition_changes.reason: The original tail-only definition permits a different otherwise-honest sequence to use the empty interval at each selected finite sample size, making the pointwise minimax infimum identically zero. A fixed finite-sample tolerance tending to zero removes this diagonal finite-prefix defect while preserving the intended uniform asymptotic notion.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed: For each \(\theta\in[-1,1]\), compute \(\widehat p_s(x)\), randomized-arm means of \(Y-\theta D\), and arm empirical variances. An arm mean with zero observations is defined to be zero; an empirical arm variance is computed with the arm-count divisor when the count is at least two. Let \(\widehat q_{sx}(\theta)\) be the corresponding plug-in cell price, replace it by \(8/e_0\) when either arm count is below two, and floor every other computed value at \(N^{-1/2}\). Define \(\widehat a(\theta)\) as the unique minimizer of \(\sum_{s,x}a_{sx}^2\widehat q_{sx}(\theta)/\{n_s\max(\widehat p_s(x),N^{-1})\}\) over \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{coll}}(p_T,\mathcal H)\).
proposed_definition_changes.reason: The original construction does not assign a value to an arm mean when its arm count is zero and does not specify the sample-variance divisor. The added conventions make the estimator a total measurable map without changing it on the probability-one asymptotic event used in the proof.

open_obligations.what_is_open: A uniform Le Cam comparison and an ordered-modulus optimizer that remains honest when the active allocation face changes.
open_obligations.obstruction: The frozen local experiment is only a construction handle. The proved quadratic modulus fixes the rate and local testing cost, but it does not control higher-order likelihood terms uniformly near face transitions or solve the bounded-parameter Gaussian confidence-set optimization.
open_obligations.attempted: The fixed-face quadratic program was dualized explicitly and reduced to a Gaussian interval-rule optimization. This does not identify a universal exact constant because the required uniform experiment convergence and transition-stable optimizer are additional claims.
open_obligations.partial_result:
On any fixed allocation face the quadratic program has the computable representation
\[
 V_{\mathrm{coll}}(P,\theta_T)=
 \sum_x\frac{p_T(x)^2}
 {\sum_{s:x\in\mathcal H_s}n_sp_s(x)/q_{sx}(\theta_T)},
\]
and the local Gaussian testing cost for displacement \(h\) is
\(h^2T_{\mathrm{coll}}(P)/2\). Thus, if the asserted Le Cam convergence is established, a facewise sharp constant is the value of the explicit optimization over measurable interval rules \(C\) in that Gaussian experiment:
\[
 \inf_C\ \sup_{t\in[-1,1]}E_t\ell(C)
 \quad\text{subject to}\quad
 \inf_{t\in[-1,1]}\Pr_t\{t\in C\}\ge1-\alpha.
\]
The rate results alone neither identify this value nor prove that an optimizer remains uniformly honest when the active allocation face changes.

proofs.proof_tex:
Assume \(K=1\) and \(p_T(x)>0\Rightarrow p_1(x)>0\) for every \(x\in\mathcal X\).  Put
\[
\mathcal I_T=\{x\in\mathcal X:p_T(x)>0\}.
\]
By the source-support definition, \(\mathcal H_1=\{x\in\mathcal X:p_1(x)>0\}\); hence the displayed implication gives \(\mathcal I_T\subseteq\mathcal H_1\).

Let \(a\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{coll}}(p_T,\mathcal H)\).  The equality constraint in the allocation-polytope definition and \(K=1\) give, cell by cell,
\[
a_{1x}=\sum_{s=1}^{1}a_{sx}=p_T(x),\qquad x\in\mathcal X.
\]
Thus there is at most one feasible allocation.  Conversely, define \(a^*_{1x}=p_T(x)\).  It is nonnegative because \(p_T\) is a mass function.  If \(x\notin\mathcal H_1\), then \(p_1(x)=0\) by the source-support definition.  The contrapositive of the assumed implication yields \(p_T(x)\le 0\); since \(p_T(x)\ge0\), this means \(p_T(x)=0\), and therefore \(a^*_{1x}=0\).  Hence \(a^*\) satisfies both the support and equality constraints in the allocation-polytope definition.  It is feasible and, by the preceding cellwise equality, unique.

Using the corrected collection-variance construction and then the unique allocation,
\[
\begin{aligned}
V_{\mathrm{coll}}(P,\theta)
&=W_{\mathrm{coll}}(P,\theta,a^*)\\
&=\sum_{x\in\mathcal H_1}
  \frac{p_T(x)^2q_{1x}(\theta)}{n_1p_1(x)}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Every denominator in this last sum is strictly positive: \(n_1\) is a positive integer, and \(p_1(x)>0\) for \(x\in\mathcal H_1\) by the source-support definition.  For \(x\in\mathcal H_1\setminus\mathcal I_T\), nonnegativity of the mass function and \(x\notin\mathcal I_T\) imply \(p_T(x)=0\), so the corresponding summand, whose denominator is positive, equals zero.  Since \(\mathcal I_T\subseteq\mathcal H_1\), deleting exactly these zero summands proves
\[
V_{\mathrm{coll}}(P,\theta)
=\sum_{x\in\mathcal I_T}
  \frac{p_T(x)^2q_{1x}(\theta)}{n_1p_1(x)}.
\]
This is the asserted one-source residual-variance formula.  Finally, wherever the quotient defining strength is defined, substituting the same variance formula at \(\theta=\theta_T\) into \(T_{\mathrm{coll}}(P)=\mu_D^2/V_{\mathrm{coll}}(P,\theta_T)\) gives the corresponding one-source strength without any further probabilistic argument.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
If \(K=1\) and \(p_T(x)>0\Rightarrow p_1(x)>0\), then the unique feasible allocation is \(a_{1x}=p_T(x)\), and
\[
V_{\mathrm{coll}}(P,\theta)
=\sum_{\substack{x\in\mathcal X\\ p_T(x)>0}}
\frac{p_T(x)^2q_{1x}(\theta)}{n_1p_1(x)}.
\]
Thus the collection allocation, variance, and, wherever its defining quotient is defined, strength reduce algebraically to their one-source residual-variance forms.

Restricting the displayed sum to positive-target-mass cells preserves the intended one-source conclusion and makes every division well typed under the stated overlap premise.

proposed_definition_changes.reason: The original double sum evaluates a conditional-variance price and divides by a cell mass even outside a source support.
